rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ IUPAC places helium in the p-block. ✅ He is 1s², i.e. s-block, but is classified in Group 18 because of closed-shell inertness.  ·  ❌ The '-ium' names are permanent. ✅ They are systematic temporary names used until a permanent name is approved (Unq → Rf).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Oganesson (Og, Z = 118) is named after Yuri Oganessian; Nihonium (Nh, 113) after Japan; Tennessine (Ts, 117) after Tennessee.  ·  IUPAC numbering 1–18 was recommended in 1988 to replace the conflicting European and American schemes.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: **Problem:** Systematic name and symbol for Z = 115. **Solution:** digits 1, 1, 5 → un + un + pent + ium = ununpentium (Uup); now permanently named Moscovium (Mc).  ·  **Problem:** Predict the oxide character of period-3 oxides from the IUPAC group classification. **Solution:** Na₂O and MgO (Groups 1, 2) basic; Al₂O₃ (13) amphoteric; SiO₂ (14) weakly acidic; P₄O₁₀ and SO₃ (15, 16) strongly acidic.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### 1. Meaning — what IUPAC is and what it decides  ·  IUPAC (International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry) is the world authority that standardises chemical nomenclature, atomic weights and the format of the periodic table. Its classification of elements covers group numbering 1–18, the s/p/d/f block division, the metal–nonmetal–metalloid grouping, collective group names, and the naming of newly discovered elements.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: The f-block spans periods 6 and 7: lanthanides (58–71) and actinides (90–103).  ·  v = V₀ sin ωt; i = I₀ sin(ωt + φ); RMS V_rms = V₀/√2.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### 2. IUPAC group numbering and collective names  ·  • 18 groups numbered left to right and 7 periods; the old European (IA, IIA, … IB) and American (IA, IB, … VIIIA) systems were replaced by 1–18 to remove ambiguity.  ·  • Collective names: Group 1 alkali metals (Li–Fr, H excluded), Group 2 alkaline earth metals (Be–Ra), Group 15 pnictogens (N–Bi), Group 16 chalcogens (O–Po), Group 17 halogens (F–At), Group 18 noble gases (He–Rn).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Z_L = ωL, Z_C = 1/(ωC)  ·  ω₀ = 1/√(LC)  ·  ❌ Hydrogen belongs unambiguously to Group 1. ✅ It is placed there but behaves partly like Group 17 and remains anomalous.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Lanthanides and actinides are d-block elements. ✅ They are f-block (inner transition); La and Ac are sometimes treated as d-block.  ·  ❌ Metalloids are a fixed chemical class. ✅ Membership is conventional (B, Si, Ge, As, Sb, Te are the usual members).  ·  ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ v = v₀ sin ωt; i = i₀ sin(ωt + φ); rms v_rms = v₀/√2..

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Helium is the standard trap: 1s² configuration (s-block) yet a Group 18 member.  ·  State the IUPAC group/period numbering and list the collective names of Groups 1, 2, 15, 16, 17 and 18.  ·  Write the systematic IUPAC name and symbol for the elements with Z = 113, 116 and 118.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Classify elements into s, p, d and f blocks and explain how the IUPAC scheme removes ambiguity.  ·  Why is helium classified in Group 18 although its configuration is 1s²?  ·  Give the IUPAC classification into metals, non-metals and metalloids with two examples each.
